title: Mini-wave commit & skill-shadowing protocol for mid-cycle capacity hedges
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Context: As Redwood scales Dedicated and Private signups, PMs are running into recurring mid-cycle request bursts that require quick staffing shifts and scoped degrades. Existing playbooks focus on broad tranche rules and surge lanes, but teams need a lightweight, repeatable protocol to: (1) accept a small number of mini-commits mid-cycle, (2) rotate short-term skill shadowing between teams, and (3) execute fast scope trims that preserve critical delivery.

Problem: Large mid-cycle reallocations are disruptive and often lack a clearly defined small-commit pathway. This results in either overcommitting (risking quality) or over-pruning (losing momentum on strategic work). We need a documented protocol that lets PMs and ENG leads make low-friction tradeoffs with predictable outcomes.

Goals:
- Provide a 30-minute decision checklist PMs can use to authorize a mini-commit.
- Define a 2-week "skill-shadow" rotation pattern so specialists can temporarily support hot work without derailing core plans.
- Specify safe scope-trim heuristics that surface non-blocking items for deferment.
- Reduce emergency all-hands reassignments by 60% for mid-cycle bursts.

Success metrics:
- % of mid-cycle requests resolved via mini-wave protocol vs ad-hoc reassignments (target: >= 70% after two cycles).
- Average time from request to commit authorization (target: <= 48 hours).
- Number of rollbacks or quality regressions tied to mid-cycle commits (target: 0 in first two cycles).

Approach / Deliverables:
1) Decision checklist (one-pager) with risk bands (green/yellow/red) and guardrails.
2) Shadowing rota template: how to pick shadowers, expected handoff notes, and re-sync cadence (1 hour daily sync + 30m EOD).
3) Scope-trim matrix: categories (safe-defer, degrade, remove) and suggested substitute deliverables.
4) Communication templates: GitHub label set, Slack cadence, and stakeholder notification matrix.
5) Post-mortem template to record lessons and to feed into Optimize recommendations.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Strict mini-commit rules reduce risk but slow down triage; we favor a lightweight checklist to keep cycle velocity.
- Shadow rotations create temporary bus factor increases; mitigate with pairing docs and short syncs.
- Automating label-based workflows reduces cognitive load but requires initial engineering support for automation (ENG dependency).

Stakeholders: PM leads (Maya Singh, Jordan Lee), Eng leads (TBD), Design (for UX impact when trimming features), Solutions & SE (customer communication), SRE (impact on SLAs).

Rollout plan:
- Week 0 (this ticket): Draft protocol and checklist; align with 2-3 cross-functional leads.
- Week 1: Pilot during Cycle 2026-W12 with two mid-sized initiatives; collect metrics.
- Week 3: Iterate checklist and publish to Confluence; add label automation via ENG-5021.
- Week 6: Bake into Cycle Planning playbook and train PM guild.

Artifacts & links:
- Draft protocol doc: https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/CAP/Mini-wave+Commit+Protocol
- Pilot tracking sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/mini-wave-pilot
- Related automation PR (ENG): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/1427
- Slack pilot channel: #cycle-mini-wave

Acceptance criteria:
- Decision checklist published in Confluence and referenced in the Cycle Planning playbook.
- At least one pilot run completed and logged in the pilot tracking sheet.
- ENG-5021 has a documented plan for label automation or a manual fallback documented.
- PM guild session scheduled to review the protocol and adoption metrics.
